plant.description: A water reservoir. Input u in [0,1] is pump duty and raises the level; the reservoir drains on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a noisy level reading.

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Primary gain magnitude and lag/delay: a mid-level long hold separates fast-large vs slow-small response and is required to size control gain and settling allowance.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with lag is correct, y rises from ~0.23 with 1-3s lag toward ~0.3-0.5, slope flattening but still >0 over last seconds unless settled; noise visible but mean trend up.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Gain direction and magnitude at high input: a second, much larger amplitude separates low-gain vs dead-zone vs reversed response and is required to size control gain.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain with drain is correct, y should stop falling and rise from ~0.07 with mean trend up over 9s, end above start and last-5s slope >=0; if y keeps falling at similar rate, positive-gain magnitude is even smaller than thought.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: High-u equilibrium and settling time: continuing same 0.8 isolates time response from amplitude change to estimate time constant and whether 0.8 can reach/hold 0.6, which sets control gain and settling allowance.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain with slow settling is right, y rises from ~0.28 toward ~0.38-0.46 over 6s with last-5s slope still clearly >0 (~0.015-0.03/s) and not flattened to zero; noise +/-0.015 but mean trend up.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: How output behaves at u=0 and drain time constant, to separate dead-zone vs low-gain and to size integral and settling allowance for control.
experiments.expected_observation: If drain-with-positive-gain is right, y falls monotonically from ~0.45 toward <0.25, last-5s mean well below start and last-5s slope negative but flattening toward zero; noise +/-0.02 but mean trend clearly down.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state gain at target-relevant input and settling rate: a u~0.7 hold from low level separates linear vs superlinear equilibrium and tests whether 0.7 drives toward 0.6, which sets feedforward and integral for control.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive nonlinear gain with slow drain is right, y rises from ~0.06 toward ~0.25-0.35 over 11s with last-5s slope clearly >0 (~0.02-0.03/s) and not settled; noise +/-0.02 but mean trend up, end still well below 0.6.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: High-u equilibrium and settling rate at 0.7 by extending the same hold to separate time response from amplitude change, which sets feedforward for 0.6 and settling allowance.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with slow settling is right, y rises from ~0.23 toward ~0.30-0.38 over 8s with last-5s slope still clearly >0 (~0.02/s) and end above start; noise +/-0.015 but mean trend up, still well below 0.6 and not settled.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Mid-input equilibrium and linearity: a step down to 0.5 from ~0.39 separates whether 0.5 holds above 0.4 or drains toward 0.3, locating the feedforward for 0.6.
experiments.expected_observation: If drain with level-dependent outflow and superlinear gain is right, starting at ~0.39 above the 0.5 equilibrium, y will flatten or fall slowly toward ~0.30-0.38 with last-5s slope near zero or slightly negative (-0.01 to +0.005) versus +0.02 at u=0.7; end below start. If y keeps rising at ~0.02/s, 0.5 equilibrium is well above 0.4 implying higher linear gain.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state input needed to hold 0.6 and local gain near target, which directly sets feedforward and feedback gain for control.
experiments.expected_observation: If superlinear positive gain is right with u=0.5 eq~0.44 and u=0.7 eq>0.6, starting at ~0.43 y will rise toward 0.50-0.55 over 6s with last-5s slope clearly >0 (~0.01-0.02/s) and end above start but still below 0.6; if u=0.6 eq is at/below 0.45, y will flatten with slope ~0.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state input to hold 0.6 and local settling rate near target, which directly sets feedforward and integral/settling time for the controller.
experiments.expected_observation: If slow first-order with eq for 0.6 near 0.50-0.55 and tau ~10s is right, starting ~0.45 y rises slowly to ~0.47-0.50 over 6s with last-5s slope 0.003-0.010/s and mean ~0.46-0.49, still well below 0.6 and not settled; noise +/-0.015 but mean trend slightly up.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state level for u~0.6-0.65 and local settling rate from ~0.50, which directly sets feedforward to hold 0.6 and integral/settling allowance.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with slow first-order settling is right and u=0.6 eq is ~0.55-0.60, starting at ~0.50 y will rise to ~0.53-0.55 over 5s with last-5s slope ~0.005-0.012/s still >0 and not settled, mean ~0.52, noise +/-0.015 but mean trend up, staying well below 0.65 and below soft limit.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Whether u=0.65 equilibrium reaches the 0.6 band and local settling rate near target, which directly sets feedforward and integral/settling allowance for the controller.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive superlinear gain with slow settling is right and u=0.65 eq is ~0.58-0.62, y starting ~0.53 will rise to ~0.54-0.56 over 4.5s with mean ~0.53-0.55 and slope still >0 ~0.004-0.008/s, noise +/-0.015 but mean trend up, staying below 0.60 and not settled; if u=0.65 eq is <=0.52, y will flatten with slope ~0.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: High-u equilibrium and settling rate at u=0.65 by extending the same hold to separate time response from amplitude change, which sets feedforward to hold 0.6 and settling allowance.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive superlinear gain with ~10-15s tau is right and u=0.65 eq is ~0.60-0.65, y starting ~0.56 will rise to ~0.58-0.60 over 4s with last-seconds slope still >0 ~0.004-0.010/s and not settled; noise +/-0.015 but mean trend up, staying below 0.65.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Delay length vs gain loss: whether low y after ~8s of u=1 is due to longer dead-time with rise imminent or weaker pump with no imminent rise, which decides between detuning for delay vs raising feedforward gain.
experiments.expected_observation: If longer ~8-12s delay is right, y at ~0.11 after ~8s of u=1 will start rising within 2-4s, ending ~0.18-0.30 with last-5s mean clearly above start and slope >0.015/s; if purely weaker gain with short delay, y would stay <0.15 with slope ~0-0.005/s and no sharp break.

ledger.statement: Increasing pump duty u increases level y with positive steady-state gain.
With u=0 the reservoir drains on its own so y decays toward a low equilibrium near zero.
Original response had 2-4s lag/delay and ~10-15s time constant, settling over ~30s, not instantly.
There is no large dead-zone: u >= 0.3 produces detectable inflow versus u=0 drain.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear across u, so a second amplitude will scale proportionally.
Holding target y=0.6 requires steady u ~0.6-0.7, above the u=0.5 equilibrium ~0.44.
Level sensor has moderate zero-mean noise ~+/-0.015 requiring averaging over seconds, not single samples.
Change is weaker actuator: same u produces smaller steady rise and slower rise slope even after delay elapsed.
Change is faster outflow: u=0 fall is faster and same u holds a lower level than before.
Change is slower response / longer transport delay (~8-12s vs 2-4s): level keeps following previous command for many seconds after a change, then responds with similar slope.
Change is sensor change: different offset or noise behaviour vs original +/-0.015 zero-mean noise.
